definition: Coh-Metrix is a computational tool that produces indices of the linguistic and discourse representations of a text.
details: Developed by Arthur C. Graesser and Danielle S. McNamara, Coh-Metrix analyzes texts on many different features.

explainer.lead: Coh-Metrix turns a piece of writing into a set of numerical indices describing its language and discourse. This gives researchers and analysts a consistent way to examine and compare texts across many features.

tiers.eli5: Coh-Metrix is like a detailed checklist for a piece of writing. Instead of giving just one opinion about the text, it produces many measurements that describe different parts of how the writing is put together.
tiers.practitioner: An analyst supplies text to Coh-Metrix and uses the resulting linguistic and discourse indices for comparison or downstream analysis. Keep the individual indices distinct: the tool reports many features, not one universal score of text quality.
tiers.paperLevel: Coh-Metrix can be described as T -> {i_1, ..., i_n}, where T is an input text and each i_k is an index of a linguistic or discourse representation. Developed by Arthur C. Graesser and Danielle S. McNamara, it characterizes a text through many features rather than reducing it to a single scalar score.

explainer.example: An analyst submits a short paragraph to Coh-Metrix and receives multiple indices describing its linguistic and discourse characteristics. The analyst can then run another paragraph through the same process and compare the two feature profiles index by index.

usedIn.name: Computational text analysis
usedIn.detail: Produces numerical feature indices that can be examined or compared across texts.

usedIn.name: Discourse analysis
usedIn.detail: Provides indices describing discourse representations in written text.

usedIn.name: Linguistic research
usedIn.detail: Supports analysis of texts across many linguistic features.

explainer.intuition: A text can be described from several angles at once. Coh-Metrix replaces an informal impression of a passage with a collection of indices covering its linguistic and discourse characteristics.
howItWorks: Coh-Metrix examines many different textual features.
It computes indices of linguistic representations.
It also computes indices of discourse representations, producing a multi-feature description of the text.
explainer.whyItMatters: It makes varied properties of a text available as explicit measurements. That supports systematic analysis and comparison without relying only on a reader's impressions.
misconceptions: It does not produce just one overall judgment of a text.
Its indices are not limited to vocabulary or grammar; they also concern discourse representations.
It is an analysis tool, not a system for writing or rewriting text.

diagram.caption: Coh-Metrix maps one input text to multiple linguistic and discourse indices.
